results.title: Marcos, MILF leader bent on signing exit agreement by 2028 — Palace
results.description: President Marcos and Moro Islamic Liberation Front Chairman Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim pledged to sign the exit agreement before the end of Marcos' term. Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro bared this following the meeting of the President and MILF leaders at Malacañan this week. "Kapuwa nangako ang pamahalaan at MILF na tatapusin ang mga natitira pang obligasyon at lalagdaan ang exit agreement bago matapos ang termino ni Pangulong Marcos Jr. (Both the government and the MILF pledged to fulfill their remaining obligations and sign the exit agreement before the end of President Marcos' term)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Friday, Nov. 6. The Palace official stressed that the step being undertaken by the government and the MILF "is not merely about fulfilling an agreement," but about providing a brighter future for families who have long yearned for peace, security, and the opportunity to live in a peaceful environment. "Nagkaisa rin ang pamahalaan at MILF na patuloy na magtulungan upang malutas ang mga hamon sa pagpapatupad ng kasunduan at matiyak na walang maiiwang pangako na hindi matutupad (The government and the MILF also agreed to continue working together to address challenges in implementing the agreement and ensure that no commitment is left unfulfilled)," Castro said. "Dahil ang tunay na kapayapaan ay hindi lamang nasusukat sa kawalan ng labanan kung hindi sa pagkakaroon ng ligtas na pamayanan, disenteng kabuhayan, pagkakaisa, tunay na pag-unlad, at pag-asang maipamana ito sa susunod na henerasyon (Because true peace is measured not only by the absence of conflict but also by the presence of safe communities, decent livelihoods, unity, genuine development, and hope that can be passed on to future generations)," Castro stressed. During the meeting, they discussed the remaining steps in advancing the peace process and the full implemention of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB). According to the Palace spokesperson, Chairman Murad reaffirmed the MILF's firm commitment to continuing the peace process and ensuring the full implementation of the CAB. The two officials, Castro added, also discussed the final phase of the decommisioning process for MILF combatants by next year. They also discussed accelerating programs that would provide livelihood opportunities and improve the quality of life of the people. The meeting at Malacañan came after the MILF chairman asked to meet the President through a letter in order to discuss the Bangsamoro peace agreement.
